subQuestions.questionText:
Various options are provided as possible answers. Choose the answer and write only the letter (A–D).

Emmah will receive a pre-determined amount invested in a … when she reaches a certain age.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C (2 marks)
A retirement annuity is a long-term investment where the invested amount, plus growth, is paid out to the investor when they reach a certain (retirement) age.

subQuestions.questionText: Non-profit companies are able to raise money through various donations. This refers to … as a criterion for contributing to the success of a business.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B (2 marks)
Capital is the criterion that refers to how a business raises funds. Non-profit companies (NPCs) typically raise capital through donations, grants and fundraising rather than through share issues.

subQuestions.questionText: Presenters use … as a visual aid to display large illustrations of products to support the core message of their presentation.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: D (2 marks)
Posters are large printed visual aids used to display illustrations of products and reinforce the core message of a presentation.

subQuestions.questionText: Chiliza Traders submitted false returns to SARS. This is known as …, a type of unethical business practice.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: A (2 marks)
Tax evasion is the illegal act of submitting false/fraudulent returns to SARS to avoid paying taxes. Tax avoidance (option C) is legal, while tax evasion is illegal and unethical.

subQuestions.questionText: Team leaders implement … as a criterion for successful team performance by providing regular feedback to their members.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B (2 marks)
Communication is the criterion that involves providing regular feedback to team members, which is essential for successful team performance.

subQuestions.questionText:
social; founders; situational; decision-making; economic; problem-solving; unlimited; transformational; bonus; limited

Companies issue … shares as compensation for unpaid dividends.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: bonus (2 marks)
Bonus shares are issued by companies to existing shareholders as compensation for unpaid/accumulated dividends, typically from retained earnings.

subQuestions.questionText: Kulsum Enterprise implements the … leadership theory as the business operates in a dynamic environment characterised by constant change.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: transformational (2 marks)
Transformational leadership theory is suited to dynamic environments characterised by constant change, as transformational leaders inspire and motivate followers to adapt to change.

subQuestions.questionText: The personal assets of partners can be sold to pay off the debts of the partnership due to bankruptcy. This refers to ... liability.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: unlimited (2 marks)
Unlimited liability means that partners are personally liable for the debts of the partnership, and their personal assets can be sold to settle business debts in the case of bankruptcy.

subQuestions.questionText: Bravo Advertisers implemented the … process when they analysed situations to identify strategies necessary for change.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: problem-solving (2 marks)
The problem-solving process involves analysing situations to identify problems and develop strategies/solutions necessary to bring about change.

subQuestions.questionText: Businesses promote … rights by providing clean water and healthcare services to their employees.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: social (2 marks)
Social rights include access to basic services such as clean water and healthcare. Businesses promote these social rights by providing such services to their employees.
subQuestions.topic: Human Rights, Inclusivity and Environmental Issues

subQuestions.questionText:
Choose a description from COLUMN B that matches a term in COLUMN A. Write only the letter (A–J).

COLUMN A: RSA Retail Savings Bonds

COLUMN B options:
A - businesses contribute time and effort to improve profitability for their investors
B - occurs when two employees have a disagreement in the workplace
C - ensures that personal protective clothing is available to all employees
D - paid by the insured when cancelling an insurance contract
E - investors receive interest annually
F - occurs when an employee has a complaint in the workplace
G - paid by the insured when a claim is lodged
H - provides employees with personal protective clothing
I - investors receive interest twice per year
J - businesses contribute time and effort to improve the wellbeing of their communities
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: I (2 marks)
RSA Retail Savings Bonds are a government-issued investment where investors receive interest twice per year (semi-annually).

subQuestions.questionText:
COLUMN A: Excess

Match with the correct description from COLUMN B (A–J as listed in 1.3.1).
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: G (2 marks)
Excess refers to the amount paid by the insured when a claim is lodged with the insurer.

subQuestions.questionText:
COLUMN A: Social responsibility

Match with the correct description from COLUMN B (A–J as listed in 1.3.1).
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: J (2 marks)
Social responsibility refers to businesses contributing time and effort to improve the wellbeing of their communities.

subQuestions.questionText:
COLUMN A: Grievance

Match with the correct description from COLUMN B (A–J as listed in 1.3.1).
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: F (2 marks)
A grievance occurs when an employee has a complaint in the workplace (distinct from conflict, which involves disagreement between two parties).

subQuestions.questionText:
COLUMN A: Health and safety representatives

Match with the correct description from COLUMN B (A–J as listed in 1.3.1).
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C (2 marks)
Health and safety representatives ensure that personal protective clothing is available to all employees in the workplace.
subQuestions.topic: Human Rights, Inclusivity and Environmental Issues

subQuestions.questionText: List FOUR types of preference shares.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 1 mark per type, mark first FOUR (4) only. Any four of the following:
- Participating preference shares
- Non-participating preference shares / Ordinary preference shares
- Cumulative preference shares
- Non-cumulative preference shares
- Redeemable preference shares
- Non-redeemable preference shares
- Convertible preference shares
- Non-convertible preference shares
[Max 4 marks]

subQuestions.questionText: Outline the functions of the Johannesburg Securities Exchange (JSE).
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks per fact (1 mark for fact, 1 mark for explanation). Any of the following:
- Gives opportunities to financial institutions to invest their surplus funds in shares.
- Serves as a barometer/indicator of economic conditions in South Africa.
- Keeps investors informed by publishing share prices daily.
- Acts as a link between investors and public companies.
- Shares are valued and assessed by experts.
- Small investors are invited to take part in the economy of the country through the buying/selling of shares.
- Venture capital market is made possible on the open market.
- Strict investment rules ensure a disciplined/orderly market for securities.
- Raises primary capital by encouraging new investments in listed companies.
- Mobilises the funds of insurance companies and other institutions.
- Regulates the market for trading in shares.
- Plans, researches and advises on investment possibilities.
- Ensures that the market operates in a transparent manner.
- Provides protection for investors through strict rules/legislation.
- Encourages short-term investment as shares can be sold at any time.
- Facilitates electronic trading of shares (STRATE).
- Channels financial resources into productive economic activities.
- Enhances job creation and increases economic growth/development.
[Max 6 marks]

subQuestions.questionText:
Read the scenario below and answer the question that follows.

VENUS ENTERPRISES (VE)
Venus Enterprises requested Mabel, the marketing manager, to present their marketing plan to stakeholders. Mabel used PowerPoint, pictures and flip charts during her presentation. She was also able to handle feedback in a non-aggressive and professional manner after her presentation.

Name TWO examples of non-verbal presentations in the scenario above.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 1 mark each, mark first TWO (2) only. Only award marks for examples given in the scenario:
- Pictures
- Flip charts
[Max 2 marks]
Note: PowerPoint is NOT non-verbal in this context.

subQuestions.questionText: Explain ways in which Mabel could handle feedback in a non-aggressive and professional manner after her presentation.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks per fact (1 mark for fact, 1 mark for explanation). Any of the following:
- Mabel/The presenter should stand throughout the feedback session.
- Be polite/confident/courteous/calm when responding to questions.
- Ensure that each question/comment is clearly understood before responding/rephrase questions if uncertain.
- The presenter should first listen and then respond.
- Provide feedback as soon as possible after the question was asked or after the session.
- Be direct/honest/sincere when responding to questions.
- Use simple language to support the examples used in the presentation.
- Keep answers short and to the point.
- Apologise/acknowledge errors/mistakes if pointed out by the audience.
- Encourage questions from the audience.
- Always address the question and not the person.
- Acknowledge good questions to motivate the audience to ask more questions.
- She should not involve herself in a debate when responding to questions.
- Mabel should not avoid the questions if she does not know the answer, but rather promise feedback on it.
- Address the full audience and not only the person who posed the question.
[Max 6 marks]

subQuestions.questionText: Discuss the role of personal attitude in successful leadership.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks per fact (1 mark for fact, 1 mark for explanation). Any of the following:
- Positive attitude releases leadership potential.
- A leader's good attitude can influence the success of the business.
- Leaders must know their strengths and weaknesses to apply their leadership styles effectively.
- A great leader understands that the right attitude will set the right atmosphere.
- Leaders' attitude may influence employees'/teams' thoughts/behaviour.
- Leaders should model the behaviour that they want to see in team members.
- Successful leaders consider the abilities/skills of team members to allocate tasks/roles effectively.
- Enthusiasm produces confidence in a leader.
- A positive attitude is critical for good leadership because good leaders will stay with the task regardless of difficulties/challenges.
- Successful employees and leaders have a constant desire to work and achieve personal/professional success.
- Leaders with a positive attitude know that there is always more to learn/space to grow.
[Max 6 marks]

subQuestions.questionText: Elaborate on the meaning of return on investment (ROI) as a factor that should be considered when making investment decisions.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks per fact (1 mark for fact, 1 mark for explanation). Any of the following:
- Refers to income from the investment, namely interest/dividends/increased capital growth on the original amount invested.
- High risk investments yield higher returns.
- Generally, there will be a direct link between risk and return.
- The return should be expressed as net after-tax gains on the investment.
- The return on investment after deduction of tax should be higher than the general increase in the initial cost of investment.
- Returns can be in the form of capital gains where the asset appreciates in value over time.
[Max 4 marks]

subQuestions.questionText:
Read the scenario below and answer the question that follows.

FORESTER TRADING (FT)
Helen, a manager at Forester Trading, applies the autocratic leadership style to lead and manage employees. She makes quick decisions without consulting employees. She offers rewards to employees who meet their daily targets. Helen's direct supervision ensures that high quality services are rendered.

Quote TWO advantages of the autocratic leadership style applied by Helen from the scenario above.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 1 mark each, mark first TWO (2) only. Only award marks for responses quoted from the scenario:
- She makes quick decisions without consulting employees.
- Helen's direct supervision ensures that high quality services are rendered.
[Max 2 marks]

subQuestions.questionText: Explain other advantages of the autocratic leadership style.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks per fact (1 mark for fact, 1 mark for explanation). Do NOT award marks for responses quoted from the scenario in 2.6.1. Any of the following:
- Work gets done in time/on schedule. The leader has certainty that decisions will be made timeously, without delays.
- Line of command/communication is clear as it is top-down/followers know exactly what to do. There is no uncertainty regarding the source of instructions, which comes directly from the leader.
- Provides strong leadership which makes new employees feel confident/safe.
- Works well in large companies where consultation with every employee is impractical.
- Clear guidance can be given to low-skilled/inexperienced/new staff. Clear/Consistent direction from the leader provides certainty to new employees.
[Max 4 marks]

subQuestions.questionText: Advise businesses on the characteristics of a public company.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks per fact. Any of the following:
- A minimum of one person is required to start a public company.
- The company name ends with the letters Ltd.
- Shareholders of a public company have limited liability.
- Public companies have legal personality and therefore have unlimited continuity.
- Requires three or more directors and three or more shareholders.
- Profits are shared in the form of dividends in proportion to the shares held.
- A public company is required to hold an Annual General Meeting (AGM).
- Register with the Registrar of Companies by drawing up a Memorandum of Incorporation.
- Raises capital by issuing shares/a prospectus to the public.
- Companies borrow capital by issuing debentures to the public.
- Auditing of financial statements is compulsory and audited statements are available to shareholders and the public.
- The new Act (Companies Act 71 of 2008) forces personal liability on directors who knowingly participated in carrying out business in a reckless/fraudulent manner.
[Max 6 marks]

subQuestions.questionText: Name FOUR human rights in the workplace.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 1 mark each, mark first FOUR (4) only. Any four of the following:
- Privacy
- Dignity
- Equity
- Freedom of speech and expression
- Information
- Safety, security and protection of life
[Max 4 marks]
subQuestions.topic: Human Rights, Inclusivity and Environmental Issues

subQuestions.questionText: Outline the causes of conflict in the workplace.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks per fact. Any of the following:
- Lack of proper communication between management and workers.
- Ignoring rules/procedures may result in disagreements and conflict.
- Management and/or workers may have different personalities/backgrounds.
- Different values/levels of knowledge/skills/experience of managers/workers.
- Little/no co-operation between internal and/or external parties/stakeholders.
- Lack of recognition for good work such as managers who may not show appreciation for extra hours worked to meet deadlines.
- Lack of employee development may increase frustration levels.
- Unfair disciplinary procedures such as favouritism/nepotism.
- Little/no support from management with regards to supplying the necessary resources.
- Leadership styles used such as autocratic leadership which may not consider workers' inputs.
- Unrealistic deadlines/Heavy workloads lead to stress resulting in conflict.
- Lack of agreement on mutual matters such as remuneration/working hours.
- Unhealthy competition/Inter-team rivalry.
- Lack of commitment/Distracted by personal objectives.
- Constant changes may cause instability.
- Lack of clarity regarding employees' roles and responsibilities.
[Max 4 marks]

subQuestions.questionText:
Read the scenario below and answer the question that follows.

NALEDI CONSULTING (NC)
Naledi Consulting requested a panel of experts to solve their complex business problem by completing a questionnaire. NC also decided that each employee should silently generate ideas before sharing them with their colleagues.

Identify TWO problem-solving techniques applied by NC. Motivate your answer by quoting from the scenario above.

| PROBLEM-SOLVING TECHNIQUES | MOTIVATIONS |
| 1. | |
| 2. | |
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks per technique, 1 mark per motivation. Mark first TWO (2) only.

Technique 1: Delphi-technique (2 marks)
Motivation: Naledi Consulting requested a panel of experts to solve their complex business problem by completing a questionnaire. (1 mark)

Technique 2: Nominal group technique (2 marks)
Motivation: NC also decided that each employee should silently generate ideas before sharing them with their colleagues. (1 mark)

Notes:
- Award marks for the problem-solving techniques even if motivations were incomplete.
- Do NOT award marks for motivations if the techniques were incorrectly identified.
[Max 6 marks]

subQuestions.questionText: Discuss the advantages of creative thinking in the workplace.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks per fact (1 mark for fact, 1 mark for explanation). Any of the following:
- Better/Unique/Unconventional ideas/solutions are generated.
- May give the business a competitive advantage if unusual/unique solutions/ideas/strategies are implemented.
- Complex business problems may be solved.
- Productivity increases as management/employees may quickly generate multiple ideas which utilises time/money more effectively.
- Managers/Employees have more confidence as they can live up to their full potential.
- Managers will be better leaders as they will be able to handle/manage change(s) positively/creatively.
- Managers/Employees can develop a completely new outlook, which may be applied to any task(s) they may do.
- Leads to more positive attitudes as managers/employees feel that they have contributed towards problem solving.
- Improves motivation amongst staff members.
- Managers/Employees have a feeling of great accomplishment and may not resist/obstruct the process.
- Managers/Employees may keep up with fast changing technology.
- Stimulates initiative from employees/managers, as they are continuously pushed out of their comfort zone.
- Creativity may lead to new inventions, which improves the general standard of living.
[Max 6 marks]

subQuestions.questionText: Explain ways in which businesses can deal with difficult employees in the workplace.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks per fact (1 mark for fact, 1 mark for explanation). Any of the following:
- Get perspective from others who have experienced the same kind of situation to be able to understand difficult employees.
- Act pro-actively if possible, as a staff/personnel problem is part of a manager's responsibilities.
- Regular meetings with supervisors/departmental heads should help to identify difficult/problem behaviour.
- Ask someone in authority for their input into the situation.
- Identify the type of personality which is creating the problem.
- Meet privately with difficult employees, so that there are no distractions.
- Make intentions and reasons for action known, so that difficult person/people feel at ease.
- Employees should be told what specific behaviours are acceptable.
- A deadline should be set for improving bad/difficult behaviour.
- The deadline date should be discussed with the difficult employee and his/her progress should be monitored.
- Guidelines for improvements should be given.
- Do not judge the person but try to understand him/her.
- Keep communication channels open/encourage employees to communicate their grievances to management.
- Build rapport/sound relations by re-establishing personal connection with colleagues.
- Help difficult employees to be realistic about the task at hand.
- Remain calm and in control of the situation.
- Treat people with respect, irrespective of whether they are capable/competent or not.
- Sometimes it may be necessary to ignore and only monitor a difficult person.
- Identify and provide an appropriate support programme to address areas of weakness.
[Max 4 marks]

subQuestions.questionText:
Read the scenario below and answer the question that follows.

PROTEA LANDSCAPING (PL)
Protea Landscaping wants to invest their surplus profit in corporate social investment (CSI) projects. The management of PL is keen to develop their employees for the sake of personal growth. They also want to prioritise rural development so that the movement of people to cities is minimised.

State TWO focus areas of corporate social investment applicable to PL in the scenario above.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 1 mark each, mark first TWO (2) only. Only award marks for responses mentioned in the scenario:
- Employees
- Rural development
[Max 2 marks]

subQuestions.questionText: Discuss the impact of CSI on communities.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks per fact (1 mark for fact, 1 mark for explanation). Mark either positives AND/OR negatives.

Positives/Advantages:
- Socio-economic issues are addressed by businesses which will improve the welfare of the community.
- Training opportunities in the community increase the possibility of appointments of members of the community.
- Implementing developmental programmes in the community improves entrepreneurial skills of communities.
- Provision of bursaries encourages communities to improve their skills.
- The standard of living of the community is uplifted/Quality of life of communities is improved.
- Better educational facilities are established in poor communities.
- Improve the health of communities by providing medical infrastructure.
- Provide rehabilitation centres to community members who have addiction problems.
- Assist communities to deal with challenges posed by HIV/Aids/unemployment/poverty.

Negatives/Disadvantages:
- Businesses are not always equipped to address social problems.
- Communities tend to be dependent on CSI programmes and struggle to take their own initiatives.
- Distribution of scarce resources to selected beneficiaries may cause discrimination.
- Some businesses only participate in CSI initiatives to raise profit.
- Businesses cannot meet the longer-term needs of society.
- The benefits of CSI programmes may not filter through to the intended groups.
- Expenditure on CSI programmes are recovered by charging higher prices.
- Businesses tend to focus on CSI programmes that do not directly benefit the community.
- Less money is available for community projects during unfavourable economic conditions.
- Consumers are not easily convinced that the business is acting in the best interest of the community.
- Businesses often appear to benefit more from CSI expenditure than the perceived benefits to the communities.
[Max 6 marks]

subQuestions.questionText:
Recommend ways in which businesses could deal with the following unprofessional business practice:

Sexual harassment
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks per fact. Any of the following:
- Provide a framework for corrective action.
- Educate employers on sexual harassment matters.
- Formulate a policy regarding sexual harassment.
- Implement internal complaints and disciplinary procedures.
- Ensure compliance with the law/business code of conduct.
- Ensure that all employees are familiar with the code of ethics of sexual abuse.
- Create a good working environment where all employees' rights and dignity are respected.
- Internal investigation should be made in order to determine the seriousness of the harassment.
- Serious cases on sexual harassment should be reported to the appropriate authorities such as SAPS.
[Max 4 marks]

subQuestions.questionText:
Recommend ways in which businesses could deal with the following unprofessional business practice:

Unauthorised use of workplace funds and resources
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks per fact. Any of the following:
- Conduct regular audits to prevent unauthorised use of funds at an early stage.
- Identify risk areas/vulnerable areas.
- Limit the number of employees having access to business funds/assets.
- Implement/Introduce fraud prevention strategies.
- Educate employees about the impact of fraud.
- Fraud prevention should be a collective responsibility of business and workers.
- Clear policies should be in place so that employees are aware of what is considered to be fraud.
- Set up systems in the organisation for the reporting of fraud and corruption.
[Max 4 marks]

questions.title: Miscellaneous Topics (Business Ventures and Business Roles)

subQuestions.questionText: Name FOUR examples of non-insurable risks.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 1 mark each, mark first FOUR (4) only. Any four of the following:
- Nuclear weapons/war/earthquakes
- Changes in fashion
- Improvement/Changes in technology
- Irrecoverable debts
- High rate of inflation
- Financial loss due to bad management
- Possible failure of a business
- Shoplifting during business hours
- Loss of income if stock is not received in time
- Losses/damages incurred because of illegal marketing activities
[Max 4 marks]

subQuestions.questionText:
Read the scenario below and answer the question that follows.

Greenview Retailers invested an amount of R20 000 at 16% simple interest over a period of two years in a fixed deposit with Unity Bank.

Calculate the interest that Greenview Retailers will receive after two years. Show ALL calculations.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Correct formula: $\text{Interest} = P \times R \times T$
Mark 2: Correct substitution: $= R20\,000 \times 16\% \times 2 \text{ years}$
Marks 3-4: Correct final answer: $= R6\,400$

Notes:
- Award full marks (4) if the answer is correct and no workings are shown.
- If formula and workings were shown correctly, but the final answer is wrong, award a maximum of THREE (3) marks.
- If the workings and the answer are incorrect, award a maximum of ONE mark for the correct formula.
[Max 4 marks]

subQuestions.questionText: Discuss the advantages of fixed deposits as a form of investment.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks per fact (1 mark for fact, 1 mark for explanation). Any of the following:
- Interest is earned at a fixed rate regardless of changes in the economic climate.
- The period of investment can be over a short/medium/long term.
- Investors can choose the investment period that suits them.
- Principal amount plus interest earned is paid out on the maturity date.
- Ensures financial discipline as investors cannot withdraw their funds before the maturity date.
- Investors earn a better return on investment than on an ordinary savings account.
- The higher the principal amount/the longer the investment period, the higher the interest rate offered.
- It has a low risk as investors are guaranteed of the final payment.
[Max 4 marks]

subQuestions.questionText: Explain how management as a criterion can contribute to the success and/or failure of a partnership.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks per fact (1 mark for fact, 1 mark for explanation). Mark either success AND/OR failure.

SUCCESS FACTORS:
- Partners are actively involved in management and may use the ideas of other partners.
- Partners have access to expertise of other partners when difficult decisions have to be made.
- Not all partners need to be actively involved in management and would rather appoint competent managers.

FAILURE FACTORS:
- Decision making can be time consuming as all partners have to be in agreement.
- Some management tasks may be neglected, as one partner may leave it to others to complete.
- Partners may disagree on how to run the business, which may lead to tension between them.
- Partners are agents of the partnership and bad management decisions may be forced onto other partners.
- Different personalities/opinions could lead to conflict/disagreements.
[Max 4 marks]

subQuestions.questionText: Advise presenters on aspects that must be considered when designing a multimedia presentation.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks per fact. Any of the following:
- Start with the text which forms the basis of the presentation.
- Select the background to complement/enhance the text.
- Choose images that may help to communicate the message.
- Include/Create graphics to assist the information which is conveyed.
- Add special effects/sound/pictures/animation to make it interesting for the audience.
- Create hyperlinks to allow quick access to other files/documents/video clips.
- Use legible font and font size so that it is easy to see/read.
- Keep slides/images/graphs/font simple by not mixing different styles/colours.
- Make sure there are no language/spelling errors.
- Use bright colours to increase visibility.
- Structure information in a logical sequence so that the audience can easily follow.
- Limit the information on each slide by using key words and not full sentences.
[Max 4 marks]

subQuestions.questionText: Name TWO elements of the triple bottom line.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 1 mark each, mark first TWO (2) only. Any two of the following:
- Profit/Economic
- People/Social
- Planet/Environment
[Max 2 marks]

subQuestions.questionText: Explain ways in which businesses can create an environment that promotes creative thinking in the workplace.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks per fact (1 mark for fact, 1 mark for explanation). Any of the following:
- Emphasise the importance of creative thinking to ensure that all staff know that management wants to hear their ideas.
- Make time for brainstorming sessions to generate new ideas such as regular workshops/build on one another's ideas.
- Place suggestion boxes around the workplace and keep communication channels open for new ideas.
- Train staff in innovative techniques/creative problem-solving skills/mind-mapping/lateral thinking.
- Encourage job swops within the organisation/Study how other businesses are doing things.
- Encourage alternative ways of working/doing things.
- Reward creativity by offering reward schemes to employees/Introduce incentives.
- Respond enthusiastically to all ideas and never let anyone feel less important.
- Make the working environment conducive to creativity/free from distraction/high noise levels.
[Max 4 marks]

subQuestions.questionText:
Read the scenario below and answer the question that follows.

VUKA TEAM (VT)
Vuka Team specialises in planning and organising social events for various clients. VT members criticise each other's ideas, as they all compete for the team leader position. Team members finally appreciate each other's differences and are able to work independently.

Identify TWO stages of team development applicable to VT. Motivate your answer by quoting from the scenario above.

| STAGES OF TEAM DEVELOPMENT | MOTIVATIONS |
| 1. | |
| 2. | |
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks per stage, 1 mark per motivation. Mark first TWO (2) only.

Stage 1: Storming (2 marks)
Motivation: VT members criticised each other's ideas, as they all compete for the team leader position. (1 mark)

Stage 2: Performing (2 marks)
Motivation: Team members finally appreciate each other's differences and are able to work independently. (1 mark)

Notes:
- Award marks for the stages of team development even if motivations were incomplete.
- Do NOT award marks for motivations if the stages were incorrectly identified.
[Max 6 marks]

subQuestions.questionText: Explain how businesses can apply transparency as a King Code principle for good corporate governance.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks per fact (1 mark for fact, 1 mark for explanation). Any of the following:
- Decisions/Actions must be clear to all stakeholders.
- Staffing and other processes should be open and transparent.
- Employees/Shareholders/Directors should be aware of the employment policies of the business.
- Auditing and other reports must be accurate/available to shareholders/employees.
- Regular audits should be done to determine the effectiveness of the business.
- Business deals should be conducted openly so that there is no hint/sign of dishonesty/corruption.
- Businesses should give details of shareholders' voting rights to them before/at the AGM.
- The board of directors must report on both the negative and positive impact of the business on the community/environment.
- The board should ensure that the company's ethics are effectively implemented.
[Max 4 marks]

subQuestions.questionText: Suggest ways in which businesses can contribute time and effort in improving the well-being of employees.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks per fact. Any of the following:
- Businesses should pay fair wages/salaries to the workers based on the nature of their work.
- Pay fair bonuses based on business earnings, as acknowledgement for hard work and commitment.
- Offer financial assistance in the case of any hardship caused by unexpected medical costs.
- Working conditions should include safety/medical/canteen facilities/benefits such as housing/leave/retirement.
- Businesses could offer annual physical/medical assessments to workers.
- Make trauma debriefing/counselling/assistance/support programmes available.
- Start a nutritional programme so that employees can enjoy one meal per day.
- Encourage employees to stay fit and healthy by getting them involved in health activities.
- Provide recreational facilities for employees.
- Provide opportunities for employees' participation in decision-making.
- Allow flexible working hours to enhance productivity.
- Make childcare facilities available on the premises for working mothers.
- Give time to staff to get involved in projects they choose.
- Businesses can provide transport for employees who work unusually long hours.
- Establish coaching and mentoring programmes for junior employees.
- Conduct team-building sessions to improve employees' morale.
- Encourage employees to attend capacity-building workshops/programmes.
[Max 4 marks]

questions.title: Section C - Business Ventures (Investment: Insurance) - Essay

subQuestions.questionText:
Businesses enjoy the benefits of different types of insurance. Some businesses overinsure while other businesses underinsure their properties. They also maintain that employees should receive benefits offered by the Unemployment Insurance Fund (UIF). The principle of indemnification/indemnity also encourages businesses to insure their various business assets.

Write an essay on insurance in which you include the following aspects:
- Outline the advantages of insurance for businesses.
- Differentiate between over-insurance and under-insurance.
- Discuss any FOUR types of benefits paid out by the Unemployment Insurance Fund.
- Advise businesses on indemnification/indemnity as a principle of insurance.
subQuestions.memoText:
ESSAY MARK ALLOCATION:
- Introduction: 2 marks
- Advantages of insurance for businesses: Max 12 marks
- Differences between over-insurance and under-insurance: Max 8 marks
- FOUR types of UIF benefits: Max 16 marks
- Indemnification/Indemnity as a principle of insurance: Max 10 marks
- Conclusion: 2 marks
- INSIGHT (LASO): 8 marks (Layout 2, Analysis 2, Synthesis 2, Originality 2)
- TOTAL: 40 (Content max 32 + Insight 8)

INTRODUCTION (Any 2 x 1 = 2 marks):
- Businesses are exposed to many risks and therefore need to take out insurance to protect themselves.
- Businesses must check/assess the market value of insured items to ensure they are not over- or under-insured.
- The UIF as a type of compulsory insurance is regulated by the state and paid in the form of levies.
- The principle of indemnification/indemnity enables businesses to make informed financial decisions.

5.2 ADVANTAGES OF INSURANCE FOR BUSINESSES (Award 2 marks each, Max 12):
- Transfers the risk from businesses to insurance companies/an insurer.
- Transfer of risk is subject to the terms and conditions of the insurance contract.
- Protects businesses against theft/loss of stock and/or damages caused by natural disasters.
- Businesses will be compensated for insurable losses, such as the destruction of property through fire.
- Business' assets such as vehicles/equipment/buildings need to be insured against damage and/or theft.
- Businesses are protected against the loss of earnings, such as strikes by employees.
- Protects businesses against dishonest employees.
- Life insurance can be taken on the life of partners in a partnership to prevent unexpected loss of capital.
- Should the services of key personnel be lost due to accidents/death, the proceeds can be paid out.
- Replacement costs for damaged machinery/equipment are very high; insurance can reduce/cover such costs.
- Protects businesses from claims made by members of the public.
- Protects businesses against losses due to death of a debtor.

5.3 DIFFERENCES BETWEEN OVER-INSURANCE AND UNDER-INSURANCE (Award 2 marks per difference, Max 8, max 4 if only one side):

OVER-INSURANCE:
- Property/Assets are insured for more than their actual/market value.
- The insurer can choose to reinstate the insured instead of making a payment.
- The insured will not receive a pay-out larger than the value of the loss at market value.

UNDER-INSURANCE:
- Property/Assets are not insured for their full market value.
- The insurer will apply the average clause to determine the amount that will be paid.
- The insured will only be paid out for the amount that the goods/assets are insured for.

5.4 TYPES OF UIF BENEFITS (Mark first FOUR only, 4 marks each = Max 16):

5.4.1 Unemployment benefits (2 marks for type, 2 for discussion):
- Employees who become unemployed/retrenched may claim within six months.
- Unemployed employees may only claim if they contributed to UIF.
- Employees enjoy these benefits until allocated funds are exhausted.
- May claim if CCMA considers their resignation as constructive dismissal.
- Must register with the Department of Labour to prove they are job seekers.
- Voluntary termination disqualifies a claim.
- Must apply within six months of termination.
- Fathers can claim for 10 consecutive days of unpaid parental leave.
- No tax is payable on unemployment benefits.

5.4.2 Illness/Sickness/Disability benefits (2+2 = 4 marks):
- Employees may receive these benefits if unable to work for more than 14 days.
- May not claim if they refuse medical treatment.
- Contributors may apply if unable to perform their duties.

5.4.3 Maternity benefits (2+2 = 4 marks):
- Pregnant contributors receive these benefits for up to 4 consecutive months.
- If miscarriage, can claim for up to six weeks/42 days.

5.4.4 Adoption benefits (2+2 = 4 marks):
- Available if legally adopted a child younger than two years.
- Employees who take unpaid leave/may receive part of their salary.
- Only one parent/partner may claim benefits.
- A contributing employee can apply for leave to look after adopted child.

5.4.5 Dependants' benefits (2+2 = 4 marks):
- Dependants may apply if breadwinner who contributed to UIF dies.
- Spouse may claim, whether employed or not.
- Must apply within six months of the death.
- Dependent children under 21 are entitled if no surviving spouse.

5.5 INDEMNIFICATION/INDEMNITY AS A PRINCIPLE OF INSURANCE (Max 10):
- Usually applies to short-term insurance, where insured is compensated for proven harm/loss.
- Insurer agrees to compensate the insured for damages/losses specified in the contract.
- Protects the insured against a specified event that may occur.
- Pay-outs are made only if the insured can prove the amount of the loss/damage.
- The amount of compensation is limited to the amount of provable loss/damage.
- The insured must be placed in the same position as before the loss; may not profit from insurance.

CONCLUSION (1 x 2 = 2 marks):
- Businesses that insure their assets remain sustainable in the market.
- Constant monitoring of insured items reduces unnecessary costs.
- Businesses should regularly review the value of their insured items.
- UIF benefits offer financial relief for businesses and employees.
- The principle of indemnification gives struggling businesses the opportunity to take out interim insurance.

INSIGHT (LASO) - 8 marks total:
- Layout (L): 2 marks - Introduction, paragraphs, conclusion present.
- Analysis/Interpretation (A): 2 marks - All headings addressed; correct interpretation (16-32 marks).
- Synthesis (S): 2 marks - Relevant decisions/facts based on the question.
- Originality (O): 2 marks - Recent examples/current trends not older than two years.

For each LASO component:
- Allocate 2 marks if all requirements met.
- Allocate 1 mark if some requirements met.
- Allocate 0 marks where requirements not met.

questions.title: Section C - Business Roles (Human Rights, Inclusivity and Environmental Issues) - Essay

subQuestions.questionText:
Businesses employ people from diverse backgrounds who take care of their own health and safety in the workplace. Businesses deal with different diversity issues so that they can enjoy the benefits of a diverse workforce. They must also promote the cultural rights of their employees in the workplace.

Write an essay on human rights, inclusivity and environmental issues in which you include the following aspects:
- Outline the responsibilities of workers in promoting human health and safety in the workplace.
- Explain ways in which businesses could deal with any THREE diversity issues in the workplace, excluding culture and religion.
- Discuss the benefits of diversity in the workplace.
- Recommend ways in which businesses could promote cultural rights in the workplace.
subQuestions.memoText:
ESSAY MARK ALLOCATION:
- Introduction: 2 marks
- Responsibilities of workers in promoting health and safety: Max 10 marks
- Dealing with THREE diversity issues: Max 16 marks
- Benefits of diversity in the workplace: Max 10 marks
- Ways to promote cultural rights: Max 10 marks
- Conclusion: 2 marks
- INSIGHT (LASO): 8 marks (Layout 2, Analysis 2, Synthesis 2, Originality 2)
- TOTAL: 40 (Content max 32 + Insight 8)

INTRODUCTION (Any 2 x 1 = 2 marks):
- Employees should take precautionary measures to promote health and safety by working with employers/safety reps.
- Sound knowledge of diversity issues enables businesses to develop strategies to deal with them.
- Dealing with diversity issues allows businesses to understand different perspectives.
- Businesses that observe cultural rights promote good team spirit.

6.2 RESPONSIBILITIES OF WORKERS IN PROMOTING HEALTH AND SAFETY (2 marks each, Max 10):
- Workers should use prescribed safety equipment.
- Report accidents to the employer as soon as possible.
- Report unsafe/unhealthy working conditions to relevant authorities/management.
- Inform the employer of any illness that may affect their ability to work.
- Workers should take care of their own health and safety in the workplace.
- Co-operate and comply with rules and procedures, such as wearing prescribed safety clothing.

6.3 DEALING WITH THREE DIVERSITY ISSUES (Mark first THREE only, 6 marks each = Max 16):
Do NOT award marks for CULTURE/RELIGION as a diversity issue. Each issue: 2 marks for naming + 4 marks for explanation.

6.3.1 Poverty (2+4 = 6):
- Employ people from different socio-economic backgrounds.
- Reward employees for services well-rendered.
- Offer subsidised meals/canteen facilities.
- Supply free uniforms to employees.
- Train employees so they can deal with retrenchment.
- Train unemployed people from local communities as part of CSI.
- Incorporate Adult Basic Education and Training (ABET).
- Ensure prices of products are affordable.
- Sponsor learnerships for unemployed people.

6.3.2 Race (2+4 = 6):
- Implement affirmative action policies as required by law.
- No discrimination based on skin colour.
- Ensure workplace is diverse by employing people from different race groups.
- Previously disadvantaged people should get preferential treatment in appointments.
- Comply with the Employment Equity Act and B-BBEE Act.

6.3.3 Gender (2+4 = 6):
- Males and females should be offered equal employment opportunities.
- Promote both men and women in managerial positions.
- Women should be employed to comply with EEA.
- Targets may be set for gender equity.
- New appointments based on skills and ability.
- Male and female employees remunerated fairly/equally.

6.3.4 Language (2+4 = 6):
- Provide training in the official language of the business.
- No worker should feel excluded in meetings.
- Employ an interpreter so everyone can understand.
- All business contracts in easy-to-understand language.
- May specify that all communications should be in one specific language.

6.3.5 Age (2+4 = 6):
- Cannot employ children under 15 years.
- Permanent workers should vary from 18 to 65 years.
- Young employees must respect and learn from older employees.
- Older employees should help young employees develop.
- Promotions should not be linked to age but to skills.
- May employ persons older than retirement age if most suitable.
- Encourage sensitivity to different perspectives.

6.3.6 Disability (2+4 = 6):
- Provide employment opportunities for physically challenged people.
- Train employees on how to deal with colleagues with disabilities.
- Be well informed on dealing with physically challenged employees.
- Accommodate physically challenged people by providing facilities/ramps.
- Ensure workers with special needs are not marginalised.
- Policies should accommodate needs of disabled people.
- Create conducive organisational culture.
- Bring in external experts to help with disability issues.
- Focus on skills/work performance, not disability.

6.4 BENEFITS OF DIVERSITY IN THE WORKPLACE (2 marks each, Max 10):
- Workforce diversity improves ability to solve problems/innovate/cultivate diverse markets.
- Employees value each other's diversity and learn to communicate across differences.
- Diversity improves morale/motivation.
- Employees demonstrate greater loyalty because they feel respected.
- Diversified workforce gives competitive advantage.
- Being respectful of differences makes good business sense/improves profitability.
- Policies/practices empower every employee to perform at full potential.
- Stakeholders evaluate businesses on how they manage diversity.
- Employees from different backgrounds bring different perspectives.
- Stimulates debate on new/improved ways of doing things.
- Better able to recognise customer needs/satisfy consumers.
- Likely to have a good public image and attract more customers.

6.5 WAYS TO PROMOTE CULTURAL RIGHTS (2 marks each, Max 10):
- Provide environment where employees are free to use their own language during free time.
- Encourage employees to attend/participate in cultural activities.
- Allow employees to provide solutions from their own cultural perspective.
- Regular cultural information sessions.
- Make provision for different cultures (food, entertainment).
- Employ people from various cultural backgrounds.
- Train employees on cultural tolerance.
- Have flexible dress-code policy allowing cultural regalia/accessories.

CONCLUSION (1 x 2 = 2 marks):
- Employees who follow safety procedures reduce workplace injuries.
- Dealing with diversity may strengthen stakeholder relations.
- Businesses enjoying diversity benefits conduct continuous research.
- Businesses promoting cultural rights attract positive media coverage.

INSIGHT (LASO) - 8 marks total:
- Layout (L): 2 marks - Introduction, paragraphs, conclusion present.
- Analysis/Interpretation (A): 2 marks - All headings addressed; correct interpretation.
- Synthesis (S): 2 marks - Relevant decisions/facts based on the question.
- Originality (O): 2 marks - Recent examples/current trends not older than two years.

For each LASO component:
- Allocate 2 marks if all requirements met.
- Allocate 1 mark if some requirements met.
- Allocate 0 marks where requirements not met.
